bank.retain_mission: Extract economically material facts about optical and AI-infrastructure supply chains: capacity and utilization, supply agreements and their terms, who supplies whom, customers and customer concentration, product specifications and qualifications, manufacturing sites and constraints, lead times and shortages, demand and its forecasts, pricing, capital expenditure, and risks that name a product, a counterparty, a site or a figure. Attribute each statement to who made it: the company whose document it is, a named executive, an analyst asking a question on a call, or a third party the document quotes; an analyst's question is not the company's statement. Preserve the difference between what was explicitly stated and what was inferred, and keep hedged and forward-looking statements hedged: a plan, an expectation or a risk is not something that happened. Keep figures, units, currencies and reporting periods exactly as stated. Ignore: safe-harbor and forward-looking-statement disclaimers; officer certifications and signature blocks; exhibit lists, exhibit indexes, tables of contents and cross-references to other parts of a filing; generic risk language that names no product, counterparty, site or figure (for example that the company may fail to compete, that the economy may weaken or that its systems may be attacked); legal and accounting boilerplate about the filing itself; and call logistics such as operator instructions, greetings and thanks.

entity_labels.description: The optical supply-chain layer or layers the fact concerns. Give every layer the fact is about, and none when it concerns none of them; a material named alone (indium phosphide, gallium arsenide, silicon photonics) is no layer, and neither is a raw material, metal or mineral (indium, gallium, germanium, rare earths) or its supply, prices or export controls: a layer is a product or a manufacturing step.

values.description: bare wafers and substrates (InP, GaAs, SOI)
laser and photonic chips: EML, DML, CW and VCSEL lasers, PICs, photodiodes
DSPs, drivers, TIAs and other electrical ICs for optics
assembly, test and contract manufacturing of optics
systems built from modules: optical transport, switches, AI clusters

bank.observations_mission: Observations are durable, specific statements about a company, or about the optical and AI-infrastructure industry, each grounded in the facts that support it. Keep one observation per company and subject (its capacity, a supply relationship, a customer dependency, a product, a constraint); make an industry-level observation only of what the facts of several companies show, and name those companies. Record who supplies or depends on whom, by name and in which direction. Keep every figure with its unit, its currency and the period it refers to. When a newer fact changes a figure, a plan or a relationship, record the change with both dates or periods (what was stated earlier and what is stated now) instead of overwriting the earlier statement. When facts contradict each other, keep both sides and say who stated each and when; never resolve a contradiction by choosing one. Keep who made each statement (the company, its executives, an analyst, a third party), and keep hedged and forward-looking statements hedged: a plan, an expectation or a risk is not an outcome. The same statement repeated in several filings, or by the same source, is one source and not corroboration: never present repetition as stronger evidence. Leave out ephemeral and generic material: boilerplate, greetings, and statements that name no company, product, counterparty or figure.
bank.reflect_mission: Form source-grounded research syntheses. Distinguish factual statements, third-party claims, model assumptions and hypotheses. Seek disconfirmation.

mental_models.name: Theme status
mental_models.source_query: What are the major documented developments in optical interconnect capacity for AI infrastructure (optical transceivers and modules, lasers, silicon photonics, indium phosphide and other photonics manufacturing), and what supporting and what opposing evidence does each rest on? Say when a development rests on a single company's own statement, and name what is missing.

mental_models.name: Bottlenecks
mental_models.source_query: Which inputs, processes or capacities in optical interconnect supply are documented as Bottlenecks: unable to meet demand within the relevant timeframe because no qualified second source or substitute exists, giving their holder pricing power? For each one, cite the evidence on demand against capacity and its timeframe, on whether a qualified second source or substitute exists or is coming, and on pricing power, and cite the evidence against it. Demand growth alone does not make a Bottleneck: list a constraint whose second-source, substitute or pricing-power evidence is missing as unconfirmed, and name what is missing.

directives.name: Cite supporting evidence
directives.content: Support every statement with the memories it rests on and cite them. Don't present a conclusion that no retrieved memory supports.

directives.name: Say when facts are missing
directives.content: When the retrieved memories don't answer the question, or answer only part of it, say so explicitly and name what is missing. Never fill a gap with general knowledge presented as evidence.

directives.name: Never fabricate figures
directives.content: Never invent or estimate contract values, customer exposure, revenue shares, capacity numbers or other figures. Report a figure only as stated in a memory, with its unit and period.

directives.name: Flag source uncertainty
directives.content: Flag uncertainty about where a statement originally came from: say whether it is the company's own statement, a third-party claim or an inference, and say when the original source is unclear.

directives.name: No trading orders
directives.content: Never give trading orders or recommendations to buy, sell or hold a security. Describe evidence and its implications only.
